Kovel Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volynska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This is the old Jewish cemetery of Kovel, first appearing on Russian maps from the late 18th century. Jews settled in Kovel from the early 16th century, gaining the right to reside on all streets in 1614; Rabbi Mordechai of Neskhizh's relocation from Toykut, documented elsewhere in this collection, brought Trisk, Neskhizh, and Ruzhin Hasidism to the city. The Jewish population reached 8,521 by 1897 and 12,758 by 1921; noted politician Chaim Pazner (1899–1981) was a resident. Following the June 1941 occupation, two ghettos held about 24,000 Jews, with 8,600 murdered in a single action on June 3–5, 1942. This cemetery was presumably demolished during WWII, with municipal service buildings later built on the site; an uninscribed memorial now stands at its entrance.
